references.text: The continuation of the text elaborating on which physical defects disqualify priests from service at the altar.
Concerns impurity that prevents priests from approaching the holy offerings, a parallel theme regarding who may serve.
The selection of Aaron and his sons for priestly service, forming the basis for Levitical requirements.
The consecration of Aaron and his sons for priestly service, requiring both physical and spiritual purity.
The sacrificial offerings are referred to as 'God's bread' (לֶחֶם אֱלֹהִים), the same expression used in 21:17.
Aaron and the Levites' responsibility for the sanctuary and priestly service.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple where only worthy priests shall serve at the altar.
The prophet criticizes priests who sacrifice animals with defects, contrasting this with the requirement for unblemished offerings and priests.
Jesus as the perfect high priest without defect, in contrast to the Levitical priests with their weaknesses.
Christ offered himself without blemish (ἄμωμον) to God, fulfilling the requirement for a flawless priesthood.
Christ as a lamb without spot or blemish (ἄμωμος), fulfilling the Old Testament requirement.
